acquisition_method.evidence: experiment types: Top-down proteomics; Affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics; Data-dependent acquisition
The mass spectrometer was operated in a data-dependent mode, with an automatic switch between MS and MS/MS scans using a top 15 method.

cleavage_agent.evidence: Proteins were digested for 16 h at 37 C with LysC/Trypsin mix at a protein:enzyme ratio of 1:100 in 50 mM TEAB pH 8.0 (Trypsin Sequence grade, Sigma; LysC, Wako).

collision_energy.evidence: Ion peptides were isolated using a 0.7 Th window and fragmented using higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy NCE of 36.

enrichment_method.evidence: Lyophilized peptides (1.5 mg) from each pool were immuno-affinity purified with the PTMScan HS Acetyl-Lysine Motif (Ac−K) kit (Cell Signaling Technology).

fractionation_method.evidence: The final mixture was desalted using a 500 mg Sep-Pak C18t cartridge (Waters) and dried prior high pH reverse phase HPLC pre-fractionation.
High pH reverse phase chromatography Labeled peptides were fractionated offline through a high pH reverse phase chromatography using an Ultimate 3000 HPLC system equipped with a sample collector.

fragmentation_method.evidence: Ion peptides were isolated using a 0.7 Th window and fragmented using higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy NCE of 36.

instrument.evidence: LC-MS/MS was done by coupling an UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano LC system to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

ionization_type.evidence: Peptides were then transferred to an EASY-Spray PepMap RSLC C18 column (Thermo) (2 µm, 75 µm x 50 cm) operated at 45 °C and separated using a 90 min effective gradient (buffer A: 0.1% FA; buffer B: 100% ACN, 0.1% FA) at a flow rate of 250 nL/min.

labeling.evidence: Peptides (500 µg) were labeled with Thermo Scientific TMTpro 18plex™ Isobaric reagents for 1 h at 25 C.
